text: Then the LORD said to me: Even if Moses and Samuel stood before me, my heart would not turn toward this people. Send them away from my presence—let them go!

And when they ask you, "Where shall we go?" tell them: This is what the LORD says: Those destined for death, to death; those for the sword, to the sword; those for famine, to famine; those for captivity, to captivity.
I will appoint over them four kinds of destroyers, declares the LORD: the sword to kill, the dogs to drag away, and the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth to devour and destroy.
I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth because of what Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, did in Jerusalem.
Who will have pity on you, Jerusalem? Who will grieve for you? Who will turn aside to ask how you are?
You have rejected me, declares the LORD; you keep going backward. So I have stretched out my hand against you and destroyed you; I am weary of relenting.
I winnowed them with a fork at the gates of the land; I bereaved them, I destroyed my people, for they would not turn from their ways.
Their widows became more numerous before me than the sand of the seas. At midday I brought a destroyer against the mothers of young men; suddenly I brought down on them anguish and terror.

The mother of seven grew faint; she gasped out her life. Her sun set while it was still day; she was disgraced and humiliated. And those of them who are left I will hand over to the sword before their enemies, declares the LORD.
Woe to me, my mother, that you gave me birth—a man of strife and contention to the whole land! I have not lent, nor have I borrowed, yet everyone curses me.
The LORD said: Surely I will set you free for a good purpose; surely I will make the enemy plead with you in a time of disaster, in a time of distress.

versions.text: The LORD said: Surely I have set you free for good. Surely I will make the enemy plead with you in a time of disaster, in a time of distress.
versions.explanation: Both clauses use the same oath formula with perfect verbs, yet the translation shifts from past ("I have set you free") to future ("I will make") without warrant. Keeping the tense consistent preserves the parallel structure and the promissory force; "for a good purpose" is also clearer than the ambiguous "for good."

text: Can iron be broken—iron from the north—or bronze?
Your wealth and your treasures I will give away as plunder, without price, because of all your sins throughout your territory.
I will make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know, for my anger has kindled a fire that will burn against you.
You know, LORD—remember me and care for me; take vengeance for me on those who persecute me. In your patience, do not take me away; know that I bear reproach for your sake.
When your words came, I ate them; your word became my joy and the delight of my heart, for I bear your name, LORD God of hosts.
I never sat in the company of revelers to make merry. I sat alone because your hand was on me, for you had filled me with indignation.
Why is my pain unending and my wound incurable, refusing to be healed? You have become to me like a deceptive brook, like waters that cannot be trusted.

versions.text: Why is my pain unending and my wound incurable, refusing to be healed? Will you be to me like a stream that fails, like waters that cannot be trusted?
versions.explanation: The infinitive absolute plus imperfect (הָיוֹ תִהְיֶה) is an emphatic assertion, not a question. Rendering it as a statement of accusation sharpens the lament and matches the Hebrew construction.

text: Therefore this is what the LORD says: If you turn back, I will restore you, and you shall stand before me. If you separate the precious from the worthless, you shall be as my mouth. Let them turn to you, but you must not turn to them.

versions.text: Therefore this is what the LORD says: If you turn back, I will restore you, and you shall stand before me. If you speak what is worthy and not what is worthless, you shall be my mouth. Let them turn to you, but you must not turn to them.
versions.explanation: תּוֹצִיא יָקָר מִזּוֹלֵל means "bring out the precious from the vile," i.e., to distinguish or extract, which the current wording flattens into simply speaking well. Also, כְּפִי is "as my mouth" (my spokesman); the comparative particle should not be dropped.

text: To this people I will make you a fortified wall of bronze; they will fight against you but will not overcome you, for I am with you to save you and deliver you, declares the LORD.

versions.text: I will make you a wall of fortified bronze to this people; they will fight against you but will not overcome you, for I am with you to save you and deliver you, declares the LORD.
versions.explanation: The adjective בְּצוּרָה (feminine) modifies חוֹמַת ("wall"), not נְחֹשֶׁת ("bronze"). The phrase means "a fortified wall of bronze," not "a wall of fortified bronze," which is not meaningful English. Fronting "To this people" also removes the awkward trailing prepositional phrase and reads better aloud.

text: I will rescue you from the hand of the wicked and redeem you from the grasp of the ruthless.
